---
title: "OPDI Papers"
---

Methodology studies behind the [Open Performance Data Initiative](https://www.eurocontrol.int/opdi).

Each paper benchmarks an OPDI algorithm against EUROCONTROL reference data and
reports what the comparison actually showed, including where a proposed method
failed.

Older papers render from a committed CSV cache — no credentials, no database, no
cluster. **The current papers render by running their analysis**: every figure
is produced by a job that declares the source files it depends on, so a figure
and the code that made it cannot drift apart. That costs cluster access to
re-render a stale page, which is the intended trade. ADEP/ADES versions 1–6 and
flight events versions 1–2 pre-date the change.

## Papers

:::: {.publication-card}
::: {.publication-info}
**[Flight events from ADS-B — version 3](flight-events-v3/index.qmd)**
&nbsp;·&nbsp; [PDF](flight-events-v3/flight-events-v3.pdf)

The one to read. Audits the four detectors behind OPDI's published flight
events, which had never been tested or compared against reference data, finds
nine defects — one of which means no take-off or landing has ever been emitted
for any aerodrome above roughly 200 ft — and adds the milestone families the
ICAO GANP indicators require, taking the reachable KPI count to nine fully and
three partially computable.

Version 3 is organised as **one chapter per event**. Each says what the event
is, how it is detected, which parameters govern it, how it changed from the
published algorithm, and whether any external source agrees with it — or why
none can. It closes three comparisons that had been coded and never run: ring
crossings against EUROCONTROL's own, runway identity against `AP_C_RWY`, and
the inter-source floor that says what "close" can mean. **The ring crossings
land inside that floor** — the detector agrees with the reference about as
closely as the reference agrees with itself.

A closing chapter designs a parameter sweep — what to optimise, against what
objective, at what cost, and which values must not be touched — without running
one.

States plainly what it has *not* measured, and reports two of its own fixes
that the data contradicted.
:::
::::

**[Departure and destination aerodromes in the OPDI flight list — version 7](adep-ades-detection-v7/index.qmd)**
&nbsp;·&nbsp; [PDF](adep-ades-detection-v7/adep-ades-detection-v7.pdf)

**The one to read if you use the data.** Written for people consuming the `ADEP`
and `ADES` columns rather than for the people building them: what they mean, how
the pipeline derives them from raw ADS-B, how often they are right, and what a
downstream analysis should do about the failure modes.

Documents the pipeline end to end for the first time, and measures every change
on two independent periods — which is what showed that three values version 6
shipped were not supported, and got them changed. Departures and arrivals use
different algorithms; candidates are chosen by exact distance rather than a
hexagon index; and a departure's null now separates "outside the observed area"
from "could not tell".
:::
::::

:::: {.publication-card}
::: {.publication-info}
**[Detecting departure and destination aerodromes from ADS-B — version 6](adep-ades-detection-v6/index.qmd)**
&nbsp;·&nbsp; [PDF](adep-ades-detection-v6/adep-ades-detection-v6.pdf)

The consolidated study. Re-measures every sweep against the pipeline as it now
stands — no number is carried over from earlier versions — and settles what
production should run. Finds that the algorithm already in service was never
tuned: its flight-level gate was fixed at FL40 and never swept, and moving it is
worth thousands of correctly named flights per three-day sample. Departures and
arrivals turn out to want different algorithms.

Written as a working record rather than for an outside reader; version 7 is the
one to send to someone who will *use* the flight list.
:::
::::

:::: {.publication-card}
::: {.publication-info}
**[Reply to the review of version 6](adep-ades-detection-v6/reply.qmd)**
&nbsp;·&nbsp; [PDF](adep-ades-detection-v6/reply.pdf)

Answers a review of version 6 point by point, in the reviewer's order, with the
numbers computed from the same committed data the review was about. Confirms
three things the review suspected and one it did not: the flight-level curve
does turn rather than rising indefinitely, the arrival tuning does hold on a
second period once the two are ranked together, `trend` genuinely could not say
"out of area" — and trajectory cleaning, step 02a of the pipeline, had been
writing a table that nothing read.

Deliberately pinned to the figures that were reviewed. Where an answer changed
once the measurements came in — out-of-area was built and then left off — the
page says so rather than being quietly revised.
:::
::::

:::: {.publication-card}
::: {.publication-info}
**[Detecting departure and destination aerodromes from ADS-B — version 5](adep-ades-detection-v5/index.qmd)**
&nbsp;·&nbsp; [PDF](adep-ades-detection-v5/adep-ades-detection-v5.pdf)

Takes the arrival deficit apart. Finds it is silence rather than error, that
most of that silence is the abstention refusing candidates it is right to
refuse, and that a bearing test — does the trajectory point at the aerodrome? —
is the first signal to beat it. Establishes why: a position difference survives
the archive's carried-forward staleness, and a rate does not, which is why
vertical rate, closing rate and the approach cone all failed.
:::
::::

:::: {.publication-card}
::: {.publication-info}
**[Thinning state vectors, and what the archive actually contains](statevector-decimation/index.qmd)**
&nbsp;·&nbsp; [PDF](statevector-decimation/statevector-decimation.pdf)

Tests whether OPDI's 5 s decimation rule — a fixed-phase `event_time % 5`
filter — loses data where reception is intermittent. It does not: the OpenSky
archive is a complete 1 Hz grid, and a correct bin-based sampler recovers 0.22%
more rows. The experiment instead finds that the grid is padded with
carried-forward positions, and that the staleness is wildly asymmetric — a
departure's first fix is fresh, while an arrival's last fix carries a position
measured a median of 190 seconds earlier.
:::
::::

:::: {.publication-card}
::: {.publication-info}
**[Detecting departure and destination aerodromes from ADS-B — version 4.5](adep-ades-detection-v4/index.qmd)**
&nbsp;·&nbsp; [PDF](adep-ades-detection-v4/adep-ades-detection-v4.pdf)

Moves detection into the OPDI pipeline itself: H3 cells as the index, exact
great-circle distance as the comparison, three modes behind one parameter.
Finds that the detection radius barely matters for coverage while the height
threshold decides almost everything — but that read on accuracy the two axes
pull the other way, so a coverage-only view overstates the case for a high
threshold. The production baseline improves enough under the new candidate
stage to overturn version 3's conclusion. Breaks results down by class of
aerodrome, which shows the method answering small aerodromes and heliports
confidently and wrongly every time. Explains the preprocessing pipeline, each
mode, and every metric from first principles.
:::
::::

:::: {.publication-card}
::: {.publication-info}
**[Detecting departure and destination aerodromes from ADS-B — version 3](adep-ades-detection-v3/index.qmd)**
&nbsp;·&nbsp; [PDF](adep-ades-detection-v3/adep-ades-detection-v3.pdf)

Finds that six of the seven most frequent departure errors were a scheduled
civil airport losing to an adjacent military airfield, and removes that class
entirely with a scheduled-service preference. Fixes an out-of-area rule that was
pre-empting valid aerodrome matches, reports out-of-area recall and precision
separately for the first time, and carries a production patch proposal for
`flights.py`.
:::
::::

:::: {.publication-card}
::: {.publication-info}
**[Detecting departure and destination aerodromes from ADS-B — version 2](adep-ades-detection-v2/index.qmd)**
&nbsp;·&nbsp; [PDF](adep-ades-detection-v2/adep-ades-detection-v2.pdf)

Corrects two accounting errors in version 1. A large share of flights have an
origin or destination outside the ingested area, and scoring those as detection
failures understated every method; and the aircraft filter was an allowlist
that discarded 47.74% of the fleet to exclude the 8.64% that are rotorcraft.
Adds trajectory extrapolation (which fails), the cleaning ablation, the
aerodrome-set sweep, an error breakdown, and a measurement of `track_id`
quality.
:::
::::

:::: {.publication-card}
::: {.publication-info}
**[Detecting departure and destination aerodromes from ADS-B — version 1](adep-ades-detection/index.qmd)**
&nbsp;·&nbsp; [PDF](adep-ades-detection/adep-ades-detection.pdf)

A comparison of seven ADEP/ADES methodologies against APDF ground truth over
two three-day samples a year apart. Finds that the production algorithm's
altitude-trend logic contributes no accuracy over a nearest-aerodrome rule on
the same flights, and that replacing it with explicit endpoint abstention
improves departure detection by 8–10 points of coverage — while the same
change fails to replicate for arrivals, and is not claimed.
:::
